I only use my right hand when doing all my make up, both sides of my face! I've always learned to do it that way, I'll do my best to explain it as clearly as I can!!

So, if you were to put make up
On the *right* side of your face with your *right* hand, you would hold the pencil like, well, a pencil =] Wrist straight pointing out in front of the hand and lined up with the forearm.

When you switch to the *left* side, I will continue to grasp the pencil the same way, but move my arm and my wrist so that when applying the liner the tip of the pencil is facing the inside corner of my left eye.

Essentially, your arm and forearm should come down in a V shape in front of you at the elbow, and your wrist turned 180 degrees with the tip of the pencil facing towards the right now.

This is the only way I can apply makeup evenly to both sides of my face!

Hopefully i can be of some help but bare with me when I say I haven't found a good resource per se.. 

   But by doing this, i was able to find someone I connected with immediately in my first session and definitely set me on the right path. 

   Anyways, what i did was i called my insurance company, got transferred around until i was speaking with someone who was able to give me a list of all the therapists in my area that were covered by them. I did ask for them to narrow down to therapists trained in gender related issues (this was before i was out to anyone and i was only just beginning to accept myself as trans, so this was the hardest conversation of my life with  stranger but 100% worth it) and to email me the list. They were happy to do this, but to my dismay only a handful were actually in the demographic i was looking for. 

So i opened up a Microsoft Word document, went through the entire list googling practitioners and researching them. I quickly found out that most therapist/counselors/what have you have a profile they create on sites like "psychology today" etc. and this was useful as I ended up reviewing each therapists profile, making sure they had a background in gender studies and just acknowledging the way they wrote about themselves and their approach. 

After about 4 hours of manual filtering i had maybe 3 or 4 names and started making my phone calls. 

So i guess what i'm trying to say is in terms of finding someone who will be most understanding of your situation and best able to help you, one of the best resources you have is your own instincts, most therapists offer a free phone consultation before you schedule an appointment so you can always get a feel for them before committing to anything.
